## Interactive: the selection trap {.smaller}

Two traits, **independent** in the whole pool. Select the top candidates by a weighted score and watch what happens.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
import json
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
pool = np.round(rng.normal(size=(400, 2)), 3).tolist()
# Plain JSON in the page: no server, no CDN, works from file://
print(f"<script>window.POOL = {json.dumps(pool)};</script>")
```

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="30%"}
```{=html}
<div id="sel-controls" style="font-size:0.65em; line-height:1.6">
  <label>Talent weight: <b id="w-out">0.50</b><br>
    <input id="w" type="range" min="0" max="1" step="0.05" value="0.5" style="width:100%"></label><br>
  <label>Selected, top %: <b id="top-out">15</b><br>
    <input id="top" type="range" min="5" max="100" step="5" value="15" style="width:100%"></label>
  <p style="margin-top:1em">
    Correlation of the two traits<br>
    whole pool: <b id="c-all"></b><br>
    selected only: <b id="c-sel" style="color:#c0392b"></b>
  </p>
</div>
```
:::

::: {.column width="70%"}
```{=html}
<svg id="sel-chart" viewBox="0 0 620 380" style="width:100%; height:auto"></svg>
<script>
(function () {
  const NS = "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg";
  const W = 620, H = 380, M = 34, LIM = 3;
  const px = x => M + (x + LIM) / (2 * LIM) * (W - 2 * M);
  const py = y => H - M - (y + LIM) / (2 * LIM) * (H - 2 * M);
  const svg = document.getElementById("sel-chart");
  const el = (tag, attrs, parent) => {
    const e = document.createElementNS(NS, tag);
    for (const k in attrs) e.setAttribute(k, attrs[k]);
    (parent || svg).appendChild(e);
    return e;
  };
  const corr = rows => {
    const n = rows.length;
    if (n < 3) return NaN;
    const mx = rows.reduce((a, r) => a + r[0], 0) / n;
    const my = rows.reduce((a, r) => a + r[1], 0) / n;
    let sxy = 0, sxx = 0, syy = 0;
    for (const r of rows) {
      sxy += (r[0] - mx) * (r[1] - my);
      sxx += (r[0] - mx) ** 2;
      syy += (r[1] - my) ** 2;
    }
    return sxy / Math.sqrt(sxx * syy);
  };

  // static frame, grid and axis labels
  el("rect", {x: M, y: M, width: W - 2 * M, height: H - 2 * M, fill: "none", stroke: "#999"});
  for (let t = -LIM + 1; t < LIM; t++) {
    el("line", {x1: px(t), y1: M, x2: px(t), y2: H - M, stroke: "#e3e6ea"});
    el("line", {x1: M, y1: py(t), x2: W - M, y2: py(t), stroke: "#e3e6ea"});
  }
  el("text", {x: W - M, y: H - 8, "text-anchor": "end", "font-size": 14, fill: "#555"}, svg).textContent = "Talent →";
  el("text", {x: M + 6, y: M + 16, "font-size": 14, fill: "#555"}, svg).textContent = "↑ Looks";
  const clip = el("clipPath", {id: "sel-clip"});
  el("rect", {x: M, y: M, width: W - 2 * M, height: H - 2 * M}, clip);
  const dots = window.POOL.map(() => el("circle", {cx: 0, cy: 0, r: 3}));
  const line = el("line", {stroke: "#7b241c", "stroke-dasharray": "5 4", "stroke-width": 1.5, "clip-path": "url(#sel-clip)"});

  const wIn = document.getElementById("w"), topIn = document.getElementById("top");
  function update() {
    const w = +wIn.value, top = +topIn.value;
    document.getElementById("w-out").textContent = w.toFixed(2);
    document.getElementById("top-out").textContent = top;
    const scores = window.POOL.map(r => w * r[0] + (1 - w) * r[1]);
    const sorted = scores.slice().sort((a, b) => a - b);
    const cutoff = sorted[Math.min(sorted.length - 1, Math.floor(sorted.length * (1 - top / 100)))];
    const chosen = [];
    window.POOL.forEach((r, i) => {
      const on = scores[i] >= cutoff;
      if (on) chosen.push(r);
      dots[i].setAttribute("cx", px(r[0]));
      dots[i].setAttribute("cy", py(r[1]));
      dots[i].setAttribute("r", on ? 4.5 : 2.8);
      dots[i].setAttribute("fill", on ? "#c0392b" : "#c4cad3");
    });
    // cutoff line: w*x + (1-w)*y = cutoff
    if (w > 0.999) {
      line.setAttribute("x1", px(cutoff)); line.setAttribute("x2", px(cutoff));
      line.setAttribute("y1", py(-LIM)); line.setAttribute("y2", py(LIM));
    } else {
      const y = x => (cutoff - w * x) / (1 - w);
      line.setAttribute("x1", px(-LIM)); line.setAttribute("y1", py(y(-LIM)));
      line.setAttribute("x2", px(LIM)); line.setAttribute("y2", py(y(LIM)));
    }
    const f = v => isNaN(v) ? "n/a" : v.toFixed(2);
    document.getElementById("c-all").textContent = f(corr(window.POOL));
    document.getElementById("c-sel").textContent = f(corr(chosen));
  }
  wIn.addEventListener("input", update);
  topIn.addEventListener("input", update);
  update();
})();
</script>
```
:::

::::

Among the selected, the traits look **negatively** related, though they are independent: the selection itself creates it (Berkson's paradox).
